notes: Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b (litert-community/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b rev 880dfa08; the seven model files and two voices pushed with adb, sha256 taken on the phone with sha256sum and equal to the Mac copies and the Hub oids) through the zoo sample app audio8_tts on LiteRT 2.2.0 (CompiledModel, Kotlin). TTS pipeline record in the Mac record's shape (#172(5), 2.2.0/2026-09-28): the artifact is the slow AR; the pipeline also runs fast_ar_int8 (10 calls per frame) and the codec decoder codec_decoder_int8_T128 on the CPU with 4 threads. The app's 'auto' codec first runs codec_decoder_fp16_T128 on the GPU and compares one fixed decode with the CPU int8 decoder: on this phone it returned the same output for real and all-zero codes (gpu_codec_check_* metrics, the load line), so the app used the CPU decoder and remembers the failure per OS build, LiteRT version and file size. That GPU leg has no row: the status vocabulary would read pass for a decoder that ignores its input (#176(4) reading; owner question in DECISIONS). RTF = generate wall / seconds of audio produced; cases = the check's three speaks of the bundled voices plus the speak with the voice registered from the first speak's wav (its codec_encoder_fp16_10s call is register_encode_*); transcription by whisper large-v3-turbo on the Mac (LiteRT heard as LightRT is the one English word error). The check runs in the instrumentation process (cpuset /foreground, evidence); the app on screen (cpuset /top-app) read RTF 1.12 for an 18-token sentence and 0.95 with a voice recorded on the phone, not entered (another harness). run1_* / run2_* = the same check on two earlier APKs of the same graphs and engine; rerun_* = the supervisor's rerun at 01:07.
